messages.subject: Simulating Point data error
parts:
Hi all,

I am trying to setup a simulation of point data, ultimately hoping to look at the effects of a group living animal on density and precision in CTDS study.

I have not used the dsims package before, so have taken the "Getting Started" vignette and used that code as a starting point to adapt it to a simple point transect analysis.

When I try to run the simulation at the end however, I receive the below:
> sim.pp <- run.simulation(sim.p)
Error in single.sim.loop(i = i, simulation = simulation, save.data = save.data,  :
  object 'dists.in.covered' not found

I am not sure where I should be adding this object and how - I didn't get the error when I ran the code as it is with the line transects comparison, so perhaps it is something specific to being point transects that I need to adjust?

I've attached my code for reference.

Many thanks
Jamie

messages.author: 875f0a74e1b42050
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Simulating Point data error
parts:
Dear Jamie,

This was a bug in the package thanks for reporting it (https://github.com/DistanceDevelopment/dsims/issues/77). The reason the bug was being triggered in your case is that there are usually no detections and if there are any then just one or two. I have fixed the bug so it will now not crash in this case (it can be re-installed now from github). However, you will instead get various warnings and errors being displayed with the current setup.

In order to increase your detections and be able to fit detection functions you will need either better detectability (detections out to greater distances), more transects or a larger population size.

I hope this helps,

Best wishes,
Laura

messages.author: 875f0a74e1b42050
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Simulating Point data error
parts:
Hi again Jaimie,

I just realised that I approached your issue as a programmer rather than a researcher.

You are trying to simulate a camera trap study.
I assume your population size of 300 is the number of groups you expect in your study region.  If so, what you are simulating at the moment then is a single moment in a camera trap study when all the animals are static. In which case it is not surprising that you often have no or very low detections. In reality, with a camera trap study, you would be recording for a period of time and your 300 animal groups would be moving around meaning that you would get more detections. 

What specific question are you trying to answer with the simulations?

Best wishes,
Laura

messages.author: 7c470552f98c92d3
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Simulating Point data error
parts:
Thanks Laura,

That makes sense. I am basically trying to get to a point where I can simulate how imprecision can result from having a group living animal, like baboons, stay in front of the cameras for long periods of time, at the same distances.

I carried out two camera trap surveys and analysed the results using both CTDS and REM. In general the actual estimates are as expected, albeit CTDS higher than REM, but the CTDS estimate in Survey 2 has significantly lower precision than that of Survey 1, or of REM in the same survey. I am trying to make sense of why this might be.

The number of sites at which baboons were detected between the two surveys were very different with Survey 1 catching them at 21/24 sites, with Survey 2 only 26/59, while the numbers were also more similar across the sites capturing them in S1, but a lot more varied in S2. My belief is that the encounter rate variance is behind the significantly higher imprecision of CTDS, and that CTDS is more responsive to this overdispersion than REM. My initial thinking was that the number of observations must cause greater variability in CTDS than REM, on account of REM only using first contacts, whereas baboons staying in front of CTs for long periods in CTDS will accumulate more observations with every passing snapshot interval/moment – something that would not occur with REM. This is basically what I am hoping to somehow simulate, but having not done similar before, and being unconvinced by another way I have tried, I thought I should start at the beginning with the dsims package and try to build up from there.

Is this something you think is feasible to do using dsims?

Thanks
Jamie
